review_type: Sentence-level editorial review, not acceptance assessment
scope: JAIR abstract through acknowledgments, checked against the LNCS main text
master_divergence: Abstract section labels, hero figure filename, checklist pointer, and acknowledgments environment differ as expected. Introduction through conclusion has no other prose divergence.

proposals.old: Define the reward asymmetry ratio $\alpha = |R^-|/R^+$ and the informativeness ratio $\eta = I_{\max}/c$ where $I_{\max} = \ln 2 - H_{\text{post}}(p)$ is the maximum expected information gain in nats, with $H_{\text{post}}(p) = -p \ln p - (1-p)\ln(1-p)$ the entropy in nats of the post-observation belief $(p, 1-p)$, so that $I_{\max}$ is the uniform prior's entropy $\ln 2$ less the entropy that one observation of accuracy $p$ leaves behind.
proposals.new: Define the reward asymmetry ratio $\alpha = |R^-|/R^+$ and the informativeness ratio $\eta = I_{\max}/c$. Here $I_{\max} = \ln 2 - H_{\text{post}}(p)$ is the maximum expected information gain in nats, and $H_{\text{post}}(p) = -p \ln p - (1-p)\ln(1-p)$ is the entropy in nats of the post-observation belief $(p, 1-p)$. Thus $I_{\max}$ is the uniform prior's entropy $\ln 2$ less the entropy remaining after one observation of accuracy $p$.
proposals.rationale: Splits a long chain of definitions into three sentences without changing any symbol, formula, unit, or interpretation.

proposals.new: The interpretation depends on the sign of $w^*_{\mathrm{thresh}}$.
proposals.rationale: Replaces an opaque phrase with the exact quantity whose sign controls the next two cases.

proposals.old: Its lower endpoint is the largest grid weight with $U(w_{\mathrm{lo}}) < B$ and its upper endpoint is the first subsequent grid weight with $U(w_{\mathrm{hi}}) \geq B$, so the bracket straddles the budget on the grid whenever a grid point at or above $B$ follows the last grid weight with usage below $B$, and its closed enclosure $[w_{\mathrm{lo}}, w_{\mathrm{hi}}]$ contains the threshold whenever the curve has no crossing of $B$ that the grid fails to resolve, between grid weights or beyond the last one (a curve whose final grid point falls back below $B$ would instead yield a non-straddling fallback flagged as such even though its threshold can exist, a shape no swept curve exhibits).
proposals.new: Its lower endpoint is the largest grid weight with $U(w_{\mathrm{lo}}) < B$ and its upper endpoint is the first subsequent grid weight with $U(w_{\mathrm{hi}}) \geq B$. The bracket therefore straddles the budget on the grid whenever a grid point at or above $B$ follows the last grid weight with usage below $B$. Its closed enclosure $[w_{\mathrm{lo}}, w_{\mathrm{hi}}]$ contains the threshold whenever the curve has no crossing of $B$ that the grid fails to resolve, between grid weights or beyond the last one. A curve whose final grid point falls back below $B$ would instead yield a non-straddling fallback flagged as such even though its threshold can exist. No swept curve exhibits that shape.
proposals.rationale: Separates endpoint definitions, the grid-straddling condition, the no-missed-crossing condition, and the fallback caveat. Every condition is retained.

proposals.old: The budget battery generally uses $100$ episodes per seed and evaluation cell, where a cell is one weight at one seed.
proposals.new: The budget battery generally uses $100$ episodes per evaluation cell, with each cell defined by one weight and one seed.
proposals.rationale: Removes the redundant per-seed modifier because the sentence already defines each cell as one weight at one seed.

proposals.old: Recall from Section~\ref{sec:experiments} that each Diagnosis test reports, noisily, which side of its own fixed split of the hidden conditions the true condition lies on, and that the two tests use different splits. The two tests are equally accurate, but because their splits differ, how much each reveals depends on how the current belief is spread across its split.
proposals.new: Each Diagnosis test noisily reports which side of its fixed partition contains the true condition, and the two tests use different partitions (Section~\ref{sec:experiments}). Although the tests are equally accurate, the information each reveals depends on the current belief over its partition.
proposals.rationale: Replaces a heavily nested description with direct sentences while retaining the fixed, differing partitions and belief dependence.

proposals.old: What the swept curves show is a step. The mean cost paid per test, $U_{\mathrm{cost}}(w)/U_{\mathrm{count}}(w)$, holds at $1.26$ from $w{=}0$ through $w{=}10$ and rises to $1.37$ and then $1.41$ only at the two largest weights, the same two weights at which the number of tests also jumps (Figure~\ref{fig:costbudget}), a $12.0\%$ spread relative to the grid-mean cost per test.
proposals.new: The swept curves show a step in mean cost per test, $U_{\mathrm{cost}}(w)/U_{\mathrm{count}}(w)$. It holds at $1.26$ from $w{=}0$ through $w{=}10$ and rises to $1.37$ and then $1.41$ only at the two largest weights, where the number of tests also jumps (Figure~\ref{fig:costbudget}). The spread is $12.0\%$ relative to the grid-mean cost per test.
proposals.rationale: Divides the observation, its numerical description, and the spread normalization into separate sentences. All values and the figure reference remain.

proposals.old: While information gain is weighted lightly, the price holds the agent to its low-weight test mix, and once $w$ is large enough to buy extra tests, test choice is driven more by what a test reveals at the current belief than by its price, which on this variant means using the expensive test more often.
proposals.new: While information gain is weighted lightly, test prices keep the agent at its low-weight test mix. Once $w$ is large enough to buy extra tests, test choice depends more on what a test reveals at the current belief than on its price. On this variant, that means using the expensive test more often.
proposals.rationale: Splits a three-clause sentence and makes clear that price refers to the test cost. The preceding sentence explicitly marking this as interpretation remains untouched.

proposals.old: Whether the two denominations also select different weights at a given budget is a separate question, and answering it requires a rule for pairing a count budget with a cost budget.
proposals.new: Testing whether the two denominations select different weights requires a rule for pairing a count budget with a cost budget.
proposals.rationale: Removes a roundabout introduction while preserving why a pairing rule is necessary.

proposals.old: At the two comparable operating points we solve for, however, they happen to land in the same crossing bracket at this grid's resolution.
proposals.new: At both tested operating points, the paired budgets select the same crossing bracket at this grid's resolution.
proposals.rationale: Replaces ambiguous pronouns and conversational phrasing with the actual objects being compared. The preceding pairing definition remains.

proposals.old: If that multiplier were the same at every weight, the pairing rule would make the two crossings coincide exactly, because a budget at a given fractional height of the count curve and the budget at the same fractional height of the cost curve would then be one and the same budget written in two units. The two curves would then cross them at the same weight.
proposals.new: If that multiplier were constant across weights, the pairing rule would express the same budget in two units. The two curves would then cross their paired budgets at the same weight.
proposals.rationale: Removes a repeated explanation of the already-defined fractional-height pairing while retaining its conditional conclusion.

proposals.old: We now estimate usage curves and shadow prices in settings where sensing and acting alternate within an episode, the interleaved observe-act settings of Section~\ref{sec:rocksample} and Section~\ref{sec:inspection}. The extension is needed because Proposition~\ref{prop:factored}'s factored-observation class admits navigation actions between observations, so that sensing and acting can alternate, whereas the observe-then-commit environments above separate observation from commitment by construction and so cannot exercise that case.
proposals.new: We now estimate usage curves and shadow prices in the interleaved observe-act settings of Sections~\ref{sec:rocksample} and~\ref{sec:inspection}, where sensing and acting alternate within an episode. These settings exercise Proposition~\ref{prop:factored}'s allowance for navigation between observations. The observe-then-commit environments above cannot exercise that case because they separate observation from commitment by construction.
proposals.rationale: Reduces repeated descriptions of interleaving and separates the motivation from the contrast with the preceding environments.

proposals.old: We measured that directly. Resampling the five seeds with replacement $2000$ times and re-solving each of the $25$ budgets of Figure~\ref{fig:stairs} on the resampled curve (\texttt{run\_\allowbreak bracket\_\allowbreak stability.py}, \texttt{results\_\allowbreak price\_\allowbreak bracket\_\allowbreak stability.csv}, with the count of every bracket outcome in \texttt{results\_\allowbreak price\_\allowbreak bracket\_\allowbreak stability\_\allowbreak counts.csv}), the reported bracket is recovered in every resample at $19$ budgets and in at least $99$ percent of resamples at $21$.
proposals.new: We measured bracket-selection stability by resampling the five seeds with replacement $2000$ times and re-solving each of the $25$ budgets of Figure~\ref{fig:stairs} on each resampled curve (\texttt{run\_\allowbreak bracket\_\allowbreak stability.py}, \texttt{results\_\allowbreak price\_\allowbreak bracket\_\allowbreak stability.csv}, with the count of every bracket outcome in \texttt{results\_\allowbreak price\_\allowbreak bracket\_\allowbreak stability\_\allowbreak counts.csv}). The reported bracket is recovered in every resample at $19$ budgets and in at least $99$ percent of resamples at $21$.
proposals.rationale: Fixes a dangling participle: the authors resample seeds, whereas the original grammar assigns that action to the reported bracket. Keeps all numerical findings and archive references.

proposals.old: In every disagreeing resample but one, the alternative is a neighbouring step of the staircase or, at Tiger's lowest and highest budgets, which lie about one standard error of usage from the two ends of its usage range, no bracket at all.

proposals.rationale: Moves an embedded explanation after the result so the alternatives can be read without interruption.

proposals.new: The cap is slack at seven budgets: every Tiger target, Bandit's three interior targets, and Diagnosis's largest. At these budgets, the reference is the unpenalized SARSOP policy, the estimated unconstrained reward optimum.

proposals.old: A separate sweep selects constants on tuning seeds under a rule recorded before the runs reported here and written after an exploratory sweep on the canonical seeds had been inspected.
